status: focused review, strict checks and all 17 installed checks passed; full baseline and source reconciliation in progress
review_scope: Focused inspection of MCP/service boundaries, model input metadata, Vapi origin authentication and bootstrap admission, voice model composition, sanitized errors, task-owner credential issuance, and package first-launch handling. Historical module review is retained separately. This is not a line-by-line audit of every repository file.

findings.result: Production dependencies are protocol/service plus transport/runtime libraries. Store is dev-only. Handler dispatches through Service; current authority is checked before tool projection/execution. No direct SQLite access in reviewed adapter production code.

Example production depends on the public client, not Connect store/service/server. Its SQLite is separately bound application state with process locks, schema checks and immutable binding verification. Read-only inspection does not claim or edit Connect server state.

MCP handler distinguishes cancelled/expired work as transport-uncertain, retains correlation IDs and directs reconciliation. The shared capacity pool limits listeners and requests to 32 with immediate overload; bounded wait reserves time for current authority and response projection. Shutdown observation distinguishes expected stop from unexpected exit.

Task runners, application journal/state, MCP and provider bootstrap responsibilities use separate modules. Larger existing top-level protocol/client files remain; no arbitrary line-count threshold is claimed. Main delegates Gate 4 task access, diagnostics and Vapi host work to CLI modules rather than implementing those workflows inline.

Shared correlation parsing rejects duplicate/malformed identifiers and mismatching aliases. Provider session correlation remains separate from authority. The async admission mutex serializes bootstrap verification while the shared MCP deadline and capacity bounds remain in force; current authority is rechecked after acquisition.

The saved assistant model and its existing tools are preserved in a per-call override. A bounded read-only lookup precedes dispatch intent; authority is checked again after lookup. Original uncertain dispatch prevents another creation. Logs select closed diagnostic stage labels rather than provider bodies or private causes.

The explicit --tasks flag adds named ownership/delegation operations without admin scope or broader recipients. Credential issuance now permits up to 64 named operations so voice and task rights fit without a wildcard; the store regression covers the upper bound. This is separate from invocation grant and task limits.

MCP input metadata and the shipped skill distinguish journal routing references from citation/message IDs. The new end-to-end MCP test rejects three wrong references before effect creation and proves exact receipt replay with the correct event ID. The final actual model uses that reference successfully.

The installation checker records first --version execution under its own 180-second budget and the existing owned-process supervisor. Application and communication deadlines are unchanged. Prior timeouts remain failures; no security-policy changes or service restart were needed for the subsequent passing launch.
